title: Late Breaking Results: Approximated LUT-Based Neural Networks for FPGA Accelerated Inference
problem: FPGA neural network acceleration via LUT-based matrix multiplication suffers from limited arithmetic intensity and memory bandwidth bottlenecks, constraining throughput and efficiency.
motivation: LUT-based approaches reduce area but face performance limitations; efficient FPGA NN acceleration is critical for edge deployment in resource-constrained scenarios.
method: LUT-MU is an approximated LUT-based matrix multiplication architecture with optimized memory distribution and pipeline design to maximize on-chip memory bandwidth utilization and arithmetic intensity.
key_novelty: Memory-optimized pipeline design for LUT-based matrix multiplication addressing FPGA bandwidth and arithmetic intensity constraints.
contributions: LUT-MU approximated matrix multiplication architecture for FPGA
Optimized memory distribution and pipelined design for bandwidth efficiency
4x throughput improvement in neural network inference
80% reduction in hardware resource consumption with only 5% accuracy loss
baselines: Standard FPGA neural network acceleration approaches
limitations: Model architectures and datasets used for accuracy evaluation not specified; generalization to larger models and precision requirements unclear.
primary_theme: Memory-optimized LUT-based neural network acceleration for FPGA edge inference
